A crisp early-morning landscape photograph of a national park trailhead in the Pacific Northwest, shrouded in the quiet stillness that comes just after dawn. A well-built wooden information kiosk stands at the start of a gravel path that curves gently before disappearing into a dense cathedral of Douglas fir and western red cedar, their massive trunks draped in emerald moss. Morning mist clings to the treetops in soft white ribbons, and shafts of pale golden light filter through the canopy, illuminating tiny motes of dust and pollen drifting in the air. The kiosk is constructed from thick pressure-treated timber with a peaked cedar-shake roof darkened by years of Pacific rain, and a wooden boot-brush station sits at its base alongside a weathered donation box and a trail register notebook dangling from a brass chain.

The main sign panel — approximately 120cm by 180cm of routed wood painted a deep forest green — dominates the face of the kiosk. Carved into the surface in cream-white bold sans-serif lettering, each character about 6cm tall, the header reads: "EAGLE RIDGE TRAIL — Cascadia Forest Reserve"

Below the header, a lighter sage-green inset panel recessed slightly into the main board displays dark brown engraved text in a clean condensed typeface, neatly organized in a single block that details: "Distance: 3.2 miles one way | Elevation Gain: 850 ft | Difficulty: Moderate | Estimated Time: 2–3 hours | Trail Surface: Packed earth, rocky sections above 2,000 ft"

Mounted below the caution placard, a brown Forest Stewardship-style directional sign with white routed lettering and carved directional arrows indicates: "← Visitor Center & Restrooms 0.5 mi | Campground Registration 0.3 mi → | Emergency Phone at Trailhead Parking Lot"

On the left timber post, a separate interpretive panel with a topographic map illustration and color-coded elevation bands is mounted at an angle for easy reading. Its explanatory text, printed in dark sepia ink on a cream background behind UV-resistant glazing, states: "You Are Here — Eagle Ridge Trail traverses old-growth forest before ascending to panoramic views of Puget Sound. Watch for bald eagles, black-tailed deer, and over 40 species of migratory birds."

At the base of the kiosk, a metal rules sign — its brown enamel surface slightly chipped at the edges from exposure — presents small white text in orderly rows: "No Bicycles Beyond This Point | Dogs Must Be Leashed | Pack Out All Trash | Permit Required for Overnight Camping — Available at Visitor Center | Trail Closes at Sunset"
